meta.find-your-setup.title.description: Browser-tab title and search-result headline of the Find your setup page (/find-your-setup). Keep the brand name 'Universal Till' unchanged; keep it short, ideally under 60 characters.

wiz.title.description: Main heading (h1) of the Find your setup wizard page. A plain, inviting question-style promise.

wiz.lede.description: Intro paragraph under the wizard heading. Sets the expectation that it is a short questionnaire (about a minute) leading to a plan, hardware and plugin recommendation. Friendly, 'we' voice.

wiz.privacy.description: Small privacy statement under the wizard intro: the page keeps nothing and sends nothing; answers only leave if the visitor emails them; analytics consent still applies to visit statistics but never includes answers. Must stay factually identical in every language.

wiz.nojs.description: Fallback notice shown only when JavaScript is off: the questions need it, so the visitor is pointed to the two options below (download or cloud account).

wiz.short.title.description: Heading of the shortcut box above the wizard for visitors who already know what they want.

wiz.short.free.description: Button label in the shortcut box: goes to the download page for the free local app.
wiz.short.free.review_exception: generic "free" branding or a call to action; the binding fee, term and data-handling statements live in the legal-tier keys (wiz.price.*, why.exit.*, hero.lede, faq.a2, foot.*)

wiz.short.free.d.description: One-line caption under the 'download the free app' shortcut. Claims: runs on the shop's own computer, works offline, no monthly fee.

wiz.short.cloud.description: Button label in the shortcut box: goes to the cloud account sign-up or sign-in at my.universaltill.com.

wiz.short.cloud.d.description: One-line caption under the cloud account shortcut: managing the shop from any browser plus the paid cloud features.

wiz.progress.description: Accessible label (screen readers only) of the wizard's progress indicator.

wiz.step.description: Progress text above each wizard question, for example 'Step 2 of 6'.
placeholders: {n} — the number of the current step, a whole number starting at 1
{total} — the total number of questions, a whole number

wiz.finish.description: Wizard button on the last question: calculate and show the recommended setup (plan, hardware, plugins).

wiz.restart.description: Button on the result screen: discard the answers and begin again at question one.

wiz.edit.description: Button on the result screen: return to the questions to change answers.

wiz.skiphint.description: Small hint under a question: answering is optional, the visitor may leave it blank and continue.

wiz.q.biz.description: Wizard question 1 (heading of the radio group): the kind of business the visitor runs.

wiz.gap.online.description: Honesty note: online ordering and web-shop sync are coming but not available, no date can be given; invites the visitor to tell us what they need.

wiz.n.cafe.description: Note for cafes: works offline so a Wi-Fi drop never stops a sale.

wiz.n.restaurant.description: Note for restaurants and bars: table plan, kitchen screen and self-order are included free.

wiz.n.retail.description: Note for shops: barcodes, variants and stock tracking free; catalogue import from CSV or Excel.

wiz.n.salon.description: Note for barbers and salons: staff accounts and shifts free; booking platform sync (such as Booksy) not available yet.

wiz.n.stall.description: Note for market stalls: runs on an Android tablet or phone, keeps selling without signal.

wiz.n.ukfiscal.description: Note for the UK: there is no fiscal-device requirement. Legal statement about UK law; keep exact.

wiz.n.deowndevice.description: Note for Germany: the visitor may stay on the Local or Local Plus plan using their own approved fiscal device. Legal-sensitive.

wiz.n.detse.description: Note for Germany: law requires a TSE (certified fiscal security device) for every business whatever till is used; Local and Local Plus users bring their own, from Shop a managed one is {tse} per month excluding VAT per main till; the free app is therefore not zero cost in Germany. {tse} is a formatted amount supplied by the page. Legal and pricing sensitive.

start.title.description: Main heading of the Getting started page.

start.lede.description: Intro paragraph: pick a device, install one small app, follow the setup wizard; no technical skills needed, and no minimum term on monthly billing (contract claim, keep exact).

start.cta.description: Button on the Getting started page: go to the download page.

start.s1.t.description: Step 1 heading, with its number: choose a device. Keep the number and the middle dot.

start.s1.d.description: Step 1 text: Universal Till is one small app that runs on hardware the shop already owns.

start.dev.pi.t.description: Device card title: Raspberry Pi (a product name).

start.dev.pi.d.description: Device card text: a Pi 4 or 5 with a touch screen makes a tidy low-cost till.

start.dev.pc.t.description: Device card title: an old PC or laptop.

start.dev.pc.d.description: Device card text: any 64-bit Windows or Linux machine works; gives an old computer a second life.

start.dev.mac.d.description: Device card text: Apple Silicon Macs (M1 and newer) run it natively.

start.dev.term.t.description: Device card title: a touch terminal.

start.dev.term.d.description: Device card text: proper POS terminals work too.

start.s2.t.description: Step 2 heading, with its number: install the app.

start.s2.d.description: Step 2 text: download the version for the device from the download page then follow the steps for the system; every install opens the setup screen.

start.win.t.description: Windows install block title, with an emoji icon. Keep the emoji.

start.win.1.description: Windows step 1: download the installer; '.exe' is a file extension, keep it.

start.win.2.description: Windows step 2: double-click and follow the wizard; it adds Start-menu and desktop shortcuts.

start.win.3.description: Windows step 3: open the app from the shortcut; the browser shows the setup screen.

start.mac.t.description: macOS install block title, with an emoji icon. Keep the emoji and 'macOS'.

start.mac.1.description: macOS step 1: download the file and unzip it.

start.mac.2.description: macOS step 2: double-click run-unitill.command; macOS blocks it the first time, so open System Settings, Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway. Menu names must match the operating system's wording in the target language; the file name stays unchanged.

start.mac.3.description: macOS step 3: the browser opens the setup screen.

start.pi.t.description: Raspberry Pi / Debian install block title, with an emoji icon.

start.pi.1.description: Pi step 1: download the .deb package for the board.

start.pi.2.description: Pi step 2: install it with the command shown. The command is code; do not translate or alter it.

start.pi.3.description: Pi step 3: open the local address to reach the setup screen. The URL is code; do not alter it.

start.lx.t.description: Other Linux install block title, with an emoji icon.

start.lx.1.description: Linux step 1: download the .tar.gz for the CPU and extract it.

start.lx.2.description: Linux step 2: run the script from the extracted folder. The command is code; do not alter it.

start.lx.3.description: Linux step 3: the browser opens the setup screen.

start.s3.t.description: Step 3 heading, with its number: follow the setup wizard.

start.s3.d.description: Step 3 text: the first start opens a short wizard.

start.w1.t.description: Setup wizard item title: your language.

start.w1.d.description: Setup wizard item text: pick the till's language, including right-to-left for Persian and Arabic.

start.w2.t.description: Setup wizard item title: your country.

start.w2.d.description: Setup wizard item text: sets currency and tax; everything can be changed later in Settings. 'Settings' should match the till's own menu name.

start.w3.t.description: Setup wizard item title: shop name and PIN.

start.w3.d.description: Setup wizard item text: name the shop and choose an admin PIN, then it is ready.

start.s4.t.description: Step 4 heading, with its number: start selling.

start.s4.d.description: Step 4 text: add a few products and ring up the first sale.

start.sell.add.d.description: Card text: add items by hand or import a CSV; Loyverse and Square exports are recognised automatically.

start.sell.ring.t.description: Card title: ring up a sale.

start.sell.ring.d.description: Card text: scan a barcode or tap a product tile, take cash or card, print or skip the receipt.

start.sell.grow.d.description: Card text: scan a QR code to add a second till; tills sync over the shop's own network, free of charge.

start.sell.plug.d.description: Card text: open the plugin store for payments, loyalty, themes and more; verified, one-click install.

start.help.d.description: Card text: the till has a built-in 'How to use the till' guide in the user's language; the download page offers a fresh copy. The quoted guide title must match the till's own help title.

manage.title.description: Heading of the cloud management section: manage the shop from anywhere.

manage.sub.description: Sub-heading: at my.universaltill.com the owner changes catalogue, modifiers and till settings and sees sales from any browser; every till picks up changes. The address is a URL, keep it.

manage.catalog.d.description: Feature text: items, prices, icons and which tills see what.

manage.reports.d.description: Feature text: sales by hour and by till, A4 printing. Ends with a coming-soon marker, keep that honesty.

manage.mods.description: Feature title: options and add-ons (modifiers such as milk choice or size).

manage.mods.d.description: Feature text: milk choices, sizes and extras with prices in one place.

tour.title.description: Heading of the screenshots tour section.

tour.sub.description: Sub-heading of the tour: real screens from a running till, not mock-ups.

tour.sale.description: Screenshot caption title: the fast touch sale screen.

tour.sale.d.description: Screenshot caption text: product tiles, scanning, one-tap payment.

tour.catalog.description: Screenshot caption title: the whole catalogue.

tour.catalog.d.description: Screenshot caption text: barcodes, variants, photos, tax and price.

tour.inventory.description: Screenshot caption title: stock you can trust.

tour.inventory.d.description: Screenshot caption text: receive, adjust, low-stock alerts, returns.

tour.reports.description: Screenshot caption title: reports and asking your till questions.

tour.reports.d.description: Screenshot caption text: sales, tax and top items, answered on the device.

tour.plugins.description: Screenshot caption title: a signed plugin store.

tour.plugins.d.description: Screenshot caption text: payments, loyalty, themes; verified, one-click.

tour.lang.description: Screenshot caption title: speaks your language.

tour.lang.d.description: Screenshot caption text: lists some supported languages and notes right-to-left support. The language list is a statement of fact about the product; keep it consistent with what ships.

hw.title.description: Heading of the Hardware section on the home page.

hw.lede.description: Paragraph of the Hardware section: Raspberry Pi, old PC, mini-PC, touch terminal; one small binary runs on all.

plugins.title.description: Heading of the Plugins teaser section on the home page.

plugins.lede.description: Paragraph of the Plugins teaser: a signed, verified marketplace for payments, integrations, loyalty, themes; one-click install; everything checked before it runs.

plugins.cta.description: Button of the Plugins teaser: go to the plugin list.

cta.title.description: Heading of the final call-to-action band.
cta.title.review_exception: 'terms' is the idiom 'on your own terms', not contract terms.

cta.lede.description: Text of the final call-to-action band: free forever for a single till; download today. Pricing claim, keep exact.

cta.btn.description: Button label of the final call-to-action band: get started. Currently not referenced by any page (kept because it is in every locale dictionary).

foot.tagline.description: Tagline in the page footer under the logo: the free, offline-first EPOS and till system.

faq.title.description: Heading of the home page FAQ section.

faq.sub.description: Sub-heading of the FAQ: explains the words EPOS, POS, till system and cash register as search terms and names the two topics, what it is and what it costs.

faq.q1.description: FAQ question 1 (also used in structured data for search engines): whether Universal Till is an EPOS system.

faq.a1.description: FAQ answer 1: yes; EPOS, POS, till system and cash register all mean the same selling software.

faq.q2.description: FAQ question 2: is it really free.
faq.q2.review_exception: generic "free" branding or a call to action; the binding fee, term and data-handling statements live in the legal-tier keys (wiz.price.*, why.exit.*, hero.lede, faq.a2, foot.*)

faq.a2.description: FAQ answer 2: the till is free forever on own hardware, open source under the MIT licence, no monthly fee for the core; paid plans only cover cloud and services. Pricing and licence claims, keep exact.

faq.q3.description: FAQ question 3: does it work without internet.

faq.a3.description: FAQ answer 3: yes, a full sale completes offline; syncing is a bonus; card payments may need a connection depending on the provider.

faq.q4.description: FAQ question 4: what hardware is needed.

faq.a4.description: FAQ answer 4: Raspberry Pi, old PC or laptop, mini-PC, touch terminal; downloads for Windows, macOS, Linux, Raspberry Pi and Android. Also states the iPhone and iPad apps are in internal testing (not on the App Store) and that a DIY till costs from about 70 pounds. Availability and price claims, keep exact.
faq.a4.review_exception: device list plus an approximate DIY hardware estimate, not a Universal Till fee or plan price

faq.q5.description: FAQ question 5: can the shop take card payments.

faq.a5.description: FAQ answer 5: yes, any card machine and processor; we are never in the money flow, no fee creep, no frozen payouts. Pricing claim.

faq.q6.description: FAQ question 6: can the shop move over from its current till.

faq.a6.description: FAQ answer 6: export from the current system and import; Loyverse, Square, SumUp and Shopify exports are recognised automatically.

android.title.description: Main heading of the Android till page.
android.title.review_exception: generic "free" branding or a call to action; the binding fee, term and data-handling statements live in the legal-tier keys (wiz.price.*, why.exit.*, hero.lede, faq.a2, foot.*)

android.lede.description: Intro paragraph of the Android page: the whole till runs on the tablet so a sale completes offline; free.

android.cta.description: Primary button on the Android page: download the Android app.

android.cta2.description: Secondary link on the Android page: jump to the set-up steps.

android.note.description: Small note under the Android buttons: Android 7.0 or newer, installed from our website, not yet from Google Play.

android.shot.description: Caption and image alt text of the Android sale-screen screenshot: the sale screen is the same on a tablet as on every other till.

android.what.title.description: Heading of the section listing what an Android tablet till offers.

android.what.same.t.description: Feature title: the same till, not a cut-down app.

android.what.same.d.description: Feature text: the Android app runs the very same till as Windows, Mac and Raspberry Pi: sale screen, catalogue, stock, receipts and so on.

android.what.offline.d.description: Feature text: everything is stored on the tablet; if Wi-Fi drops the status bar says so and sales continue.

android.what.bt.t.description: Feature title: Bluetooth scanners and scales.

android.what.bt.d.description: Feature text: pair a Bluetooth barcode scanner or scale from inside the till; Android asks once to allow Bluetooth.

android.what.multi.t.description: Feature title: one till or several.

android.what.multi.d.description: Feature text: an Android tablet can be the main till or join another till on the shop's network; sales sync between them.

android.what.kiosk.d.description: Feature text: set a tablet to self-order so customers order themselves; the till asks Android to pin the screen, which blocks the Home and Back buttons.

android.what.update.t.description: Feature title: updates from inside the till.

android.what.update.d.description: Feature text: when a new version is out tap the update chip and confirm in Android's own installer; the first time Android also asks for permission. 'Update chip' must match the till's status-bar label.

android.setup.title.description: Heading of the Android set-up section.

android.setup.steps.t.description: Sub-heading above the numbered Android set-up steps.

android.setup.s1.description: Android step 1: open the download page on the tablet and tap the Android app; most tablets need the 64-bit version which the page picks automatically.

android.setup.s2.description: Android step 2: allow installing from unknown sources when Android asks; Play Protect may say it has not seen the app before, tap Scan app, then continue. Button names must match Android's wording in the target language.

android.setup.s3.description: Android step 3: open Universal Till and follow the setup (language, country, shop name), then add products.

android.limits.t.description: Heading of the limitations list on the Android page.

android.limits.i1.description: Limitation: the app is not on Google Play yet, it is downloaded from this website.

android.limits.i2.description: Limitation: Android does not let an app replace itself silently, so every update needs one tap in Android's installer.

android.limits.i3.description: Limitation: an Android till joined to a main till does not update itself to match; install the new version by hand.

android.limits.i4.description: Limitation: card payments go through the shop's own card machine and provider, which may need its own connection.

android.limits.i5.description: Limitation: screen pinning is Android's standard pin; it starts only after the user accepts Android's prompt, and someone who knows Android's unpin gesture can leave it. Security-relevant, keep accurate.

android.faq.title.description: Heading of the FAQ on the Android page.

android.faq.q1.description: Android FAQ question 1: does the tablet need Wi-Fi or mobile data.

android.faq.a1.description: Android FAQ answer 1: not to sell; a sale completes with no connection; Wi-Fi is needed to work with other tills on the shop's network.

android.faq.q2.description: Android FAQ question 2: can an Android tablet work alongside a Windows or Raspberry Pi till.

android.faq.a2.description: Android FAQ answer 2: yes, every version runs the same till; the tablet can be the main till or join a main till on another platform.

android.faq.q3.description: Android FAQ question 3: is it on Google Play.

android.faq.a3.description: Android FAQ answer 3: not yet; download from our site; Android warns the first time because the app is from outside Google Play, which is expected.

android.faq.q4.description: Android FAQ question 4: which tablets does it run on.
